description: Behavioural obligations for the §8.7.2 OPTIONAL SSE stream and the §15 truthfulness rules it must not undermine — the zombie-socket problem, bounded holds, provisional delivery, and the schema-inexpressible hold<=freshness cross-field relation (JSON Schema's dialect cannot compare two advertised fields; checked here).
obligation: ZOMBIE-SOCKET TRUTHFULNESS (§8.7.2/§16.2): (1) An open SSE connection MUST NOT by itself renew the session lease or presence — SSE is unidirectional and TCP half-open, so a merely-open socket is not liveness evidence. A session held ONLY by an open stream with no client-originated activity past the freshness window reads `offline` and its lease lapses (the §14.2 bounce then fires, dp-022) — the zombie socket cannot hold a session `online`. (2) The Hub MUST bound each stream hold and close the stream at the bound; the client's RECONNECT is the renewal. A healthy client reconnecting at the advertised bound stays `online` continuously and renews at least once per freshness window. (3) The bound for a given hold is the LESSER of the advertised `inbound.stream_max_hold_seconds` and a point sufficiently before the presenting session's lease expiry that an immediate reconnect lands within the lease — the margin is implementation-defined but MUST be nonzero (closing exactly AT expiry hands the client a renewal moment it can only use after the lease is immutably terminal). A Hub MAY additionally clamp requested `ttl_seconds` UP to `sessions.min_ttl_seconds` compatible with its holds. CROSS-FIELD (§8.0/§8.7.2): (4) The advertised `inbound.stream_max_hold_seconds` MUST be <= `presence.freshness_seconds` — a hold longer than the freshness window would read a healthy-but-idle held stream as offline mid-hold. Schema-inexpressible (cross-object comparison); a conformant Hub's capability document MUST satisfy it and its tests MUST assert it. PROVISIONAL STREAM DELIVERY (§8.7.2/§15.1): (5) A stream push starts the entry's visibility window exactly like a drain claim, but ONLY client-originated receipt evidence advances the delivery track — a drain response stamps `delivered`; a server-originated stream push does NOT. A stream-pushed, never-acked entry reverts to queued-visible after the visibility window and its delivery track never left `queued` — at-least-once preserved, and a push into a dead socket changes nothing the sender is told. PRESENCE TRUTHFULNESS (§15.1): (6) The Hub MUST NOT report `online` absent qualifying client-originated activity within the window, and MUST NOT advance a delivery track absent client-originated receipt evidence (drain response, ack, or §9.4-verified webhook 2xx) — optimistic reporting is non-conformant. (7) Addressed-message reachability (the §8.1 snapshot, session/fleet reads) derives from SESSION-BEARING activity only: a destination whose only consumer drains session-less MUST NOT read `online` there (it can never be shown a v0.5 entry — online-but-undeliverable is the banned false belief), while the v0.4 directive-presence derivation is unchanged (no regression for session-less pollers). (8) Long-poll drain remains the conformance floor — a pull-only Hub is conformant; the stream is advertised capability, not a requirement.
